chapter: Telephone reels: blues and Bessie Smith
title: Hearing early jazz, and writing his first blues and 'Empty Bed Blues'
summary: He cannot name the first great jazz musician he heard, says his first blues was never recorded, and played what he felt, thinking of Bessie Smith.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Do you remember the first really great jazz musician that you ever heard or jazz singer?
I really don't. All I know is that I heard so daggoned many that -- I couldn't tell you which was

who. So many of them played the blues, and I've been all over, and -- from New Orleans to the coast of the west coast (inaudible). I've heard the blues played by many different types of people. And so it's their interpretation of it. But the blues -- the blues, regardless of who plays them, they're still the blues.

Uh-huh. Do you -- you don't remember how you happened to write -- do you remember how you happened to -- I should say, make it positive. Do you remember how you happened to write your very first blues song?
Well, my very first blues song was never recorded.
No, it was just a blues song.
What is the name of it.
I don't even remember it. I have it somewhere at home there.
Uh-huh. Did you write it out of a personal experience of your own?

Uh-huh. Did you write -- when you first began writing, I know how easily music comes into your mind, you know, that you think in music and in poetry, but I know that, for instance, a lot of writing that I did and maybe still do comes out of, you know, an emotional experience. And was -- is that how it started for you, like you had to get something
Well, no. No, I never did it that way. I just sat down and played it. That was it. That's the way I felt. I played the way I felt. It came out that way.
Uh-huh. You -- so then, for instance, when you wrote 'Empty Bed Blues', was that something you were inventing?
Well, it was something that I thought would be nice for Bessie Smith to use.
And it certainly was, wasn't it?
Yeah, I was right that time.
